1	# PLAN — Automated self-healing with a diagnostic memory
     2	
     3	Build plan for the `rocket-fuel/self-heal` cycle. Vision and non-negotiables live in
     4	`rocket-fuel/self-heal/VTO.md`; deferred items in `rocket-fuel/self-heal/DEFERRED.md`.
     5	This plan is the subject of the Same Page Meeting and is revised on the record until
     6	`VERDICT: SAME PAGE`. **Revision 1** (as submitted).
     7	
     8	## Starting point (facts, verified 2026-09-14 on this checkout)
     9	
    10	- `scripts/self_heal.py` (4,067 bytes): six idempotent repair steps (`pip install -e .`,
    11	  `ruff check --fix --extend-exclude claude .` + `ruff format --exclude claude .`,
    12	  `pytest --snapshot-update`, pinned type-stub install, `pip-compile` when
    13	  `requirements.in` exists, optional doc/badge regeneration). After each step it compares
    14	  `git status --porcelain` before/after and, only when *that* step changed something,
    15	  runs `check_health()`; `sys.exit(0)` on the first step that both changed the tree and
    16	  passed healthcheck, else `sys.exit(1)`. It takes no arguments, reads no config, has no
    17	  concept of a failure identity, and keeps no record of having run.
    18	- `scripts/healthcheck.py` (2,325 bytes): `ruff check .`, `pyright`, `pytest --cov=.
    19	  --cov-fail-under=90`, the `run_dca.py --demo --report --now 2026-08-03T15:45` smoke test
    20	  into a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` outside the worktree, and `pip-audit --requirement
    21	  requirements-dev.txt --strict`. Prints the failing command's stdout/stderr; exit 0/1.
    22	- `.github/workflows/self-heal.yml`: triggers are `schedule` (`0 3 * * 1`),
    23	  `workflow_dispatch`, and `workflow_run` on CI completion. The job `if:` admits only
    24	  `schedule` on `refs/heads/main` and `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'failure'` and

    27	  `concurrency` group `selfheal-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress` false on main.

    32	  contradicting `workflow_dispatch:` line three lines below it — see Finding A.**

    52	  `scripts/workflow_policy.py` (timeout / concurrency / `persist-credentials` policy over
    53	  `.github/workflows/*.yml`).
    54	- Redaction precedent: `dca_console_jobs.redact()` masks env values whose **names** match
    55	  `SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|API_KEY|ACCOUNT_NUMBER`, labelled secrets, and any 6–12 digit run.
    56	- `pyproject.toml` `[tool.setuptools] py-modules` is an explicit flat list with a comment

    58	  `scripts/*.py` ship automatically, but new top-level config needs a `data-files` entry.
    59	- Test layout: `tests/test_<module>.py` for core modules, `scripts/tests/test_<script>.py`
    60	  for scripts (`test_healthcheck.py` and `test_model_usage_log.py` already exist there).
    61	  `scripts/tests` is **outside** the root pytest sweep and is run separately.
    62	
    63	## Architecture
    64	
    65	Three cooperating engines, one config file, one committed hand-off tree. The split follows
    66	interview Q2: **local collector, CI healer.**
    67	
    68	```
    69	  LOCAL MAC (launchd, once daily)                 GITHUB ACTIONS (repair sandbox)
    70	  ────────────────────────────────                ──────────────────────────────
    71	  scripts/self_heal_daily.py
    72	    1. diagnostic_collector.py  ── sweeps ──▶ raw incidents (gitignored)
    73	    2. incident_fingerprint.py  ── reduces ─▶ stable fingerprint + redacted excerpt
    74	    3. incident_ledger.py       ── records ─▶ novelty verdict, attempt history
    75	    4. self_heal_governor.py    ── gates ──▶ DISPATCH or a reason code
    76	    5. on DISPATCH: commit sanitized
    77	       digest + ledger mirror to the
    78	       `self-heal-diagnostics` branch,  ────push───▶  workflow_run/push trigger
    79	       push                                          │
    80	                                                     ▼
    81	                                          .github/workflows/self-heal.yml
    82	                                            a. re-run self_heal_governor.py  ← same caps,
    83	                                               against the committed ledger     enforced twice
    84	                                            b. scripts/self_heal.py repair steps
    85	                                            c. scripts/healthcheck.py
    86	                                            d. open labeled PR (never merge)
    87	                                            e. write the outcome back to the
    88	                                               ledger on the diagnostics branch
    89	```
    90	
    91	The governor runs **on both sides**. Local enforcement stops a wasted push; CI enforcement
    92	is the one that actually binds, because a hosted run triggered by any path (including the
    93	weekly cron) must obey the same caps.
    94	
    95	### Why a dedicated `self-heal-diagnostics` branch, not `main`
    96	
    97	A daily digest commit to `main` would add a commit per day to the audit history of a live
    98	trading repository and would race the operator's own concurrent commits (a known hazard in
    99	this checkout). A long-lived orphan branch carrying only `diagnostics/` keeps the hand-off
   100	auditable, keeps `main`'s history clean, and makes "self-heal reacting to its own output"
   101	structurally impossible to confuse with a real change to `main`.
   102	
   103	## Component 1 — `scripts/incident_fingerprint.py`
   104	
   105	Pure functions, no I/O. Two public entry points.
   106	
   107	`normalize(text: str) -> str` strips, in order:
   108	
   109	| Pattern | Replacement | Why |
   110	|---|---|---|
   111	| ISO-8601 and `HH:MM:SS` timestamps | `<TS>` | same crash, different second |
   112	| `0x[0-9a-f]{6,}` | `<ADDR>` | object addresses |
   113	| `/Users/<name>/…`, `$HOME` | `~` | machine-specific, and a PII leak |
   114	| absolute paths inside the checkout | repo-relative | CI path ≠ local path |
   115	| `pid=\d+`, `PID \d+` | `<PID>` | |
   116	| `\b\d{6,12}\b` | `<NUM>` | account-shaped literals; see redaction |
   117	| `shard_\d+` | `shard_<N>` | one MPS bug, four shards, one fingerprint |
   118	| trailing whitespace, ANSI SGR escapes | removed | |
   119	
   120	`fingerprint(kind, frames, message) -> str` returns the first 16 hex chars of
   121	`sha256(kind + "\x00" + "\x00".join(frames[:5]) + "\x00" + normalize(message))`, where
   122	`frames` are only the **repo-owned** traceback frames (path under the checkout, third-party
   123	and stdlib frames dropped) each reduced to `relpath:function` — deliberately *without* the
   124	line number, so a fix that shifts lines elsewhere in the file does not mint a new identity
   125	for an unchanged bug.
   126	
   127	Rationale for dropping line numbers: the alternative — including them — makes every
   128	unrelated edit above the crash site look like a brand-new failure, which is exactly the
   129	runaway-work condition the governor exists to prevent.
   130	
   131	## Component 2 — `scripts/diagnostic_collector.py`
   132	
   133	One `Source` protocol, five registered implementations, each a pure `scan(root) ->
   134	list[Incident]`:
   135	
   136	1. `octopus_shard` — `analysis/real-octopus-run/shard_*/stdout.log`: lines matching
   137	   `^RUNTIME FAILURE \((?P<kind>\w+)\):` and any Python traceback block.
   138	2. `cron_artifacts` — `$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT/**/run_state.json` in a terminal failure
   139	   state, plus `$DCA_ATTEMPT_LOG_ROOT` failed-start markers.
   140	3. `console_jobs` — `cron_tracking/console/**` job output with a nonzero exit.
   141	4. `ci_runs` — `gh run list --branch main --status failure --limit 20 --json …`. Skipped
   142	   with a recorded reason when `gh` is absent or unauthenticated; never fatal.
   143	5. `healthcheck` — runs `scripts/healthcheck.py`, captures stdout/stderr on nonzero exit,
   144	   attributes each failing command as its own incident.
   145	
   146	Every `Incident` is a frozen dataclass serialized to JSON:
   147	
   148	```json
   149	{"fingerprint":"a1b2…","source":"octopus_shard","origin":"analysis/real-octopus-run/shard_1/stdout.log",
   150	 "kind":"NotImplementedError","signature":"…normalized one-liner…","excerpt":"…redacted, ≤4 KiB…",
   151	 "severity":"high","first_seen_utc":"…","last_seen_utc":"…","occurrences":3,"collector_version":1}
   152	```
   153	
   154	**Redaction runs on `excerpt` and `signature` before either is written anywhere**, using a
   155	`redact()` lifted from `dca_console_jobs.py`'s rules and extended with: the literal value of
   156	`$ROBINHOOD_AGENTIC_ACCOUNT_NUMBER` when set, every env value whose *name* matches the
   157	existing regex, `~` substitution, and the `\b\d{6,12}\b` rule. A unit test asserts a
   158	synthetic account number planted in a fixture never appears in any emitted artifact.
   159	
   160	Raw, unredacted incidents are written under `$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT/self_heal/incidents/`
   161	— already gitignored — so the operator can still read the full crash locally.
   162	
   163	## Component 3 — `scripts/incident_ledger.py`
   164	
   165	Append-only JSONL under `$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT/self_heal/ledger/incidents.jsonl`, with a
   166	sanitized mirror at `diagnostics/ledger.jsonl` on the diagnostics branch. Every append takes
   167	`file_lock.cross_process_lock`. A compacted `diagnostics/index.json` holds current state per
   168	fingerprint so a reader need not replay the whole log.
   169	
   170	Per-fingerprint state machine:
   171	
   172	```
   173	   new ──dispatch──▶ dispatched ──PR merged & healthcheck green──▶ repaired
   174	    │                    │
   175	    │                    ├──repair produced no diff, or CI still red──▶ refused ──▶ (back to new, attempts+1)
   176	    │                    │
   177	    └────────────────────┴──attempts > max_attempts_per_fingerprint──▶ quarantined (terminal)
   178	```
   179	
   180	`quarantined` is terminal and is **never** dispatched again. It is surfaced in the digest

181	and in the daily report so a human sees it. Clearing it is an explicit operator action
   182	(`--unquarantine <fingerprint>`).
   183	
   184	Novelty verdict: a fingerprint is dispatch-eligible iff state ∈ {`new`, `refused`} **and**
   185	`attempts < max_attempts_per_fingerprint`.
   186	
   187	## Component 4 — `scripts/self_heal_governor.py` (the limits)
   188	
   189	`evaluate(now, ledger, config, spend) -> Decision`. `Decision` is
   190	`(dispatch: bool, fingerprint: str | None, reason: str)`, where `reason` is a constant from
   191	a new `scripts/self_heal_reasons.py` following the `scripts/reason_codes.py` house pattern.
   192	Checks run in this fixed order and **short-circuit on the first refusal**:
   193	
   194	| # | Gate | Config key | Default | Refusal reason |
   195	|---|---|---|---|---|
   196	| 0 | Kill switch | `enabled` / `$DCA_SELF_HEAL_DISABLED` | `true` / unset | `DISABLED` |
   197	| 1 | Self-origin drop | — | — | `SELF_ORIGIN_DROPPED` |
   198	| 2 | Daily rate limit | `max_runs_per_day` | **1** | `RATE_LIMITED_DAILY` |
   199	| 3 | Circuit breaker | `consecutive_failure_threshold`, `breaker_cooldown_hours` | **3**, **72** | `BREAKER_OPEN` |
   200	| 4 | Per-fingerprint attempts | `max_attempts_per_fingerprint` | **3** | `FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED` |
   201	| 5 | Token/USD budget | `daily_token_budget`, `daily_usd_budget`, `monthly_usd_budget` | **200000**, **2.00**, **20.00** | `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_TOKENS` / `_USD` |
   202	| 6 | Actions minutes | `monthly_actions_minutes` | **300** | `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_MINUTES` |
   203	| 7 | Wall clock | `max_wall_clock_seconds` | **1800** | `WALL_CLOCK_EXCEEDED` |
   204	| 8 | Novelty | — | — | `NO_NOVEL_INCIDENTS` |
   205	
   206	Every evaluation — dispatch or refusal — is appended to the ledger with its reason, so the
   207	answer to "why did nothing happen yesterday?" is always in the record.
   208	
   209	**Loop prevention, stated explicitly.** Four independent mechanisms, any one of which alone
   210	halts a runaway:
   211	
   212	- Gate 2 caps *dispatches per day* at 1. Even a pathological collector that mints a new
   213	  fingerprint every minute gets one dispatch.
   214	- Gate 4 caps *attempts per failure identity* at 3 for that identity's entire lifetime, then
   215	  quarantines it permanently.
   216	- Gate 3 trips a breaker after 3 consecutive unsuccessful dispatches regardless of
   217	  fingerprint, and holds it open for 72 hours or until an explicit human reset.
   218	- Gate 1 drops any incident whose origin path is under `diagnostics/`, whose branch matches
   219	  `selfheal-*`, or whose signature names a self-heal module — so the loop cannot observe
   220	  and react to its own exhaust. (The workflow's existing `!startsWith(github.ref_name,
   221	  'selfheal-')` guard covers the ref; this covers the *content*.)
   222	
   223	Fail-closed: an unparseable `config/self_heal.json`, an unreadable ledger, a clock that has
   224	moved backwards relative to the last ledger entry, or a governor exception all produce
   225	`dispatch=False` with an explicit reason. There is no code path where an error yields
   226	permission.
   227	
   228	## Component 5 — `scripts/self_heal_spend.py`
   229	
   230	Append-only `$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT/self_heal/spend/YYYY-MM.jsonl`, mirrored sanitized to
   231	`diagnostics/spend/YYYY-MM.jsonl`, schema `schemas/self_heal_spend.schema.json`. One entry
   232	per governor evaluation that reached dispatch:
   233	
   234	`{run_id, fingerprint, started_utc, ended_utc, wall_clock_seconds, tokens_in, tokens_out,
   235	usd_estimate, actions_minutes, outcome, reason}`
   236	
   237	`usd_estimate` is computed from a `config/self_heal.json` price table so it stays honest
   238	when rates change; when a dispatch consumed no model call (the deterministic repair path,
   239	which is the default) the token fields are `0` and the entry still records wall clock and
   240	Actions minutes. Budget gates read this file; they never trust an in-memory counter.
   241	
   242	## Component 6 — `config/self_heal.json` + `schemas/self_heal.schema.json`
   243	
   244	Every number in the governor table above lives here; raising the daily cap later is a
   245	one-line config edit, exactly as the operator asked. Schema validation is added to
   246	`tests/test_config_invariants.py`, the existing gate. `pyproject.toml` gains the config
   247	under `[tool.setuptools.data-files]` (hard invariant — a missed entry silently falls back to
   248	defaults in an installed wheel).
   249	
   250	## Component 7 — wiring
   251	
   252	- `scripts/self_heal_daily.py`: the local orchestrator. Flags `--dry-run` (print the
   253	  decision, touch nothing), `--now` (deterministic testing), `--report`.
   254	- `deploy/launchd/render_self_heal_agent.py`: renders `com.all-stock-dca.self-heal.plist`
   255	  (label, once-daily `StartCalendarInterval`, `.venv/bin/python`, no secrets embedded),
   256	  modeled directly on the existing `render_console_agent.py` including its `sys.path.insert(1, …)`
   257	  precedence comment. The rendered plist is gitignored by the existing `deploy/launchd/*.plist`
   258	  rule.
   259	- `.github/workflows/self-heal.yml`: add a `push` trigger on the `self-heal-diagnostics`
   260	  branch; insert a governor step as the **first** step after checkout, whose refusal exits
   261	  the job cleanly (not as a failure — a refused run is a correct outcome, and a red X here
   262	  would itself trigger the reactive path); add an outcome-writeback step. `timeout-minutes`
   263	  stays and is cross-checked against `max_wall_clock_seconds`.
   264	  `python scripts/workflow_policy.py` must stay green.
   265	
   266	## Rocks
   267	
   268	Seven, at the cap. Each carries a proof command a human runs; per Audit rules every proof
   269	also re-runs the existing suite so nothing regresses.
   270	
   271	**Rock 1 — Fingerprint + redaction.** `scripts/incident_fingerprint.py`,
   272	`scripts/self_heal_redact.py`.
   273	*Non-goals:* no collection, no I/O, no ledger.
   274	*Proof:* `.venv/bin/python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_incident_fingerprint.py scripts/tests/test_self_heal_redact.py -q` — including a golden test that the real shard-1 MPS line fingerprints identically when its timestamp, home path and `shard_N` differ, and a test that a planted 9-digit account number never survives redaction — plus `ruff check .`.
   275	
   276	**Rock 2 — Collector.** `scripts/diagnostic_collector.py` with all five sources.
   277	*Non-goals:* no ledger, no governor, no git operations.
   278	*Proof:* `.venv/bin/python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_diagnostic_collector.py -q` and `.venv/bin/python -m scripts.diagnostic_collector --dry-run --json` over a fixture tree, plus `ruff check .`.
   279	
   280	**Rock 3 — Ledger + novelty.** `scripts/incident_ledger.py`.
   281	*Non-goals:* no governor limits, no dispatch.
   282	*Proof:* `.venv/bin/python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_incident_ledger.py -q` — asserting a re-collected identical incident is not novel, a changed one is, the state machine's terminal `quarantined` is never re-dispatched, and concurrent appends under `cross_process_lock` do not interleave — plus `ruff check .`.
   283	
   284	**Rock 4 — Governor + config + schema.** `scripts/self_heal_governor.py`,
   285	`scripts/self_heal_reasons.py`, `config/self_heal.json`, `schemas/self_heal.schema.json`.
   286	*Non-goals:* no spend ledger yet (gates 5–6 read an injected spend summary), no wiring.
   287	*Proof:* `.venv/bin/python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_self_heal_governor.py -q` with one test per gate 0–8 in isolation and one fail-closed test per corruption mode, **and** `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config_invariants.py -q`, plus `ruff check .`.
   288	
   289	**Rock 5 — Spend ledger.** `scripts/self_heal_spend.py`, `schemas/self_heal_spend.schema.json`.
   290	*Non-goals:* no live cost API; the price table is config.
   291	*Proof:* `.venv/bin/python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_self_heal_spend.py -q` including month-rollover reset and a budget-exhausted refusal writing no dispatch, plus `ruff check .`.
   292	
   293	**Rock 6 — Local orchestrator + launchd agent.** `scripts/self_heal_daily.py`,
   294	`deploy/launchd/render_self_heal_agent.py`.
   295	*Non-goals:* does not modify the workflow.
   296	*Proof:* `.venv/bin/python scripts/self_heal_daily.py --dry-run --now 2026-09-14T04:00` prints a deterministic decision and exits 0 having written nothing; `.venv/bin/python deploy/launchd/render_self_heal_agent.py --print` emits a valid plist containing no secret; `.venv/bin/python -m pytest scripts/tests/test_self_heal_daily.py -q`.
   297	
   298	**Rock 7 — CI wiring, docs, packaging.** `.github/workflows/self-heal.yml`,

1	# VTO — Automated self-healing with a diagnostic memory
     2	
     3	Vision/Traction document for the `rocket-fuel/self-heal` cycle (Kickoff, 2026-09-14).
     4	Namespaced under `rocket-fuel/self-heal/` so the completed `rocket-fuel/hosted-console`
     5	cycle's root `PLAN.md` / `VTO.md` / `SAME-PAGE-LOG.md` / `DEFERRED.md` stay intact as the
     6	historical record (operator decision, interview Q1).
     7	
     8	## What
     9	
    10	A closed loop with four parts:
    11	
    12	1. **Collect.** Every diagnostic this system already emits — Wondrous Octopus shard crash
    13	   logs, `cron_tracking/` run artifacts, console job output, failed CI runs, and the
    14	   `scripts/healthcheck.py` gate's own output — swept into one normalized, redacted
    15	   incident store on a fixed daily cadence.
    16	2. **Remember.** Each incident is reduced to a stable **fingerprint** and written to an
    17	   append-only ledger that knows what has been seen before, how many times it has been
    18	   attacked, and how those attempts ended.
    19	3. **Heal.** Only genuinely *new* (or still-unrepaired) fingerprints are dispatched to the
    20	   repair pipeline. A repair opens a pull request; it never merges itself.
    21	4. **Govern.** One fail-closed gate stands in front of the dispatch step and enforces every
    22	   limit the operator asked for: one run per day, a spend ceiling, a per-failure attempt
    23	   cap, and a circuit breaker.
    24	
    25	## Why now
    26	
    27	The repair pipeline already exists (`scripts/self_heal.py`, `scripts/healthcheck.py`,
    28	`.github/workflows/self-heal.yml`) but it is **blind and forgetful**:
    29	
    30	- **Blind.** `.gitignore` excludes `*.log` and `cron_tracking/`, so the two richest crash
    31	  sources on this machine are invisible to a hosted runner. Today's live example: shard 1's
    32	  `stdout.log` ends in `RUNTIME FAILURE (NotImplementedError): aten::_nested_tensor_from_mask_left_aligned
    33	  is not currently implemented for the MPS device`. Nothing in the self-heal path can see
    34	  that line, so nothing will ever act on it.
    35	- **Forgetful.** The workflow reacts to a CI conclusion. It has no memory of which failure
    36	  it already tried to fix, so the same failure can be re-attacked indefinitely and a fixed
    37	  one leaves no record that it was fixed.
    38	- **Ungoverned.** There is a weekly cron and a reactive `workflow_run` trigger, and no
    39	  ceiling of any kind on how often the loop may fire, how much it may spend, or how many
    40	  times it may retry the same thing.
    41	
    42	## Who
    43	
    44	A single operator (the repository owner), on one Mac that holds the artifact tree, with
    45	GitHub Actions as the repair sandbox.
    46	
    47	## Success criteria for this cycle
    48	
    49	- A crash written to any configured source is, within one day, present in the incident
    50	  store with a stable fingerprint and a redacted excerpt.
    51	- Re-running the collector over unchanged sources produces **zero** new incidents.
    52	- The self-heal dispatch cannot fire twice in one UTC day, and raising that ceiling later
    53	  is a config edit, not a code change.
    54	- A single failure fingerprint can consume at most a bounded, configured number of repair
    55	  attempts in its entire lifetime, after which it is quarantined and surfaced to a human.
    56	- Every refusal to dispatch names a machine-readable reason code and is written to the
    57	  ledger.
    58	- No self-heal artifact committed to this repository ever contains the brokerage account
    59	  number, an absolute home path, or any value from a `SECRET`/`TOKEN`/`PASSWORD`/`API_KEY`
    60	  named environment variable.
    61	
    62	## Non-negotiables
    63	
    64	- **Standard library only** in everything that runs at core-DCA runtime. Python ≥3.11.
    65	- **The account-number invariant holds.** `tests/test_config_invariants.py` greps for
    66	  account-shaped literals; sanitized digests are committed to a public repository, so
    67	  redaction is a correctness requirement, not a nicety.
    68	- **Fail closed.** If the governor cannot prove a limit is satisfied, it refuses to
    69	  dispatch. An unreadable ledger, an unparseable config, or a clock it cannot trust are all
    70	  refusals, never permissions.
    71	- **Nothing merges itself.** Repairs land as labeled pull requests for human review
    72	  (interview Q4). This repository drives live trading.
    73	- **Self-heal must never react to its own output.** Incidents originating from self-heal's
    74	  own artifacts, branches, or pull requests are dropped before the ledger sees them.
    75	- **The existing trust boundary in `self-heal.yml` is preserved.** No new
    76	  `workflow_dispatch` path into a job holding `contents: write`.
    77	- **No new runtime third-party dependency.** `gh` and `git` are the only external binaries,
    78	  and both are already assumed by the existing workflow.
    79	
    80	## Out of scope this cycle
    81	
    82	Recorded in `DEFERRED.md`. Headlines: auto-merge of any repair, agent-driven repair of live
    83	trading logic, repairing the sibling research subprojects' own suites, and multi-machine
    84	coordination.

131	## Hard invariants
   132	
   133	These are enforced by tests or by fail-closed runtime code. Violating one fails the build.
   134	
   135	- **Secrets.** The brokerage account number lives only in `$ROBINHOOD_AGENTIC_ACCOUNT_NUMBER`
   136	  and is referenced in config as `"${ROBINHOOD_AGENTIC_ACCOUNT_NUMBER}"`, resolved by
   137	  `dca_config.expand_config_env`. Never inline an account-shaped literal in config, source,
   138	  docs, or tests — `test_config_invariants.py` greps for it and fails. `conftest.py` assigns a
   139	  synthetic `999000111` unconditionally so the suite is hermetic even on a machine that exports
   140	  a real value.
   141	- **Config ↔ constant parity.** `near_close_dca.BUDGET_TIERS`, `ACTIVE_TICKERS`, and
   142	  `EXCLUDED_TICKERS` must agree with `config/budgets.json` and `config/tickers.json`. Some code
   143	  paths build a bare `StrategyConfig()` and never see the JSON, so a drift changes behavior on
   144	  some paths and not others. `test_config_invariants.py` is the enforcement.
   145	- **No hard-coded absolute paths.** Artifact roots come from `dca_paths.stream_root(...)` /
   146	  `cron_tracking_root()` (honouring `$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT`); ticker history from
   147	  `dca_ticker_paths.configured_ticker_history_dir()`. Never write a literal `/home/user/...`.
   148	- **New top-level module or config file ⇒ update `pyproject.toml`.** Add the module to
   149	  `[tool.setuptools] py-modules` and any newly-read config to `[tool.setuptools.data-files]`,
   150	  or it works from a checkout and `ImportError`s / silently falls back to defaults in an
   151	  installed wheel. The existing comment trail in that file records every time this was missed.
   152	- **The CLI is dry-run only.** `run_dca.main()` returns 2 if `config.dry_run` is False, if
   153	  `--slot` is passed, or if `--demo` is absent. Live runs go through `run_pipeline()` /
   154	  `run_slot()` with wired callables, never the CLI.
   155	- **Fail closed, always.** Config loading rejects duplicate JSON keys, rejects valid-JSON-that-
   156	  is-not-an-object, and treats a missing account number as a hard error rather than an empty
   157	  substitution. When reconciliation cannot be proven complete, the run must not submit.

   113	## Wondrous Octopus and adjacent prediction tools
   114	
   115	Wondrous Octopus is the whole-market, walk-forward OHLC forecasting project.
   116	Its models are persistence, quantile GBM, and neural PyTorch Octopus. It predicts
   117	the next trading row using prior data, scores matured forecasts, supports
   118	online updates, and reports uncertainty and encoder-health diagnostics.

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Cross-process advisory file lock: POSIX ``flock`` fast path, portable fallback.
     3	
     4	Several reliability engines need a *cross-process* critical section -- the run
     5	ledger serializes sequence allocation + append, and the scheduler lease
     6	serializes its check-then-mutate operations. Both ran on ``fcntl.flock`` on
     7	POSIX and silently degraded to a no-op wherever ``fcntl`` was unavailable, so
     8	concurrent processes on a non-POSIX host lost the guarantee entirely.
     9	
    10	This module is the single implementation both use:
    11	
    12	  * On POSIX, an advisory ``fcntl.flock`` on a sidecar lock file, acquired
    13	    non-blocking in a poll loop so ``timeout_seconds`` is honored (a plain
    14	    blocking ``flock`` would wait forever on a hung holder). The kernel releases
    15	    the lock automatically if the holder crashes, so it can never wedge.
    16	  * Where ``fcntl`` is absent, a portable ``O_CREAT | O_EXCL`` lock file: exactly
    17	    one writer can create it, the rest spin until it is released. It deliberately
    18	    does NOT reclaim a lock by mtime or pid. Reclaiming a lock that is actually
    19	    still live would let two writers into the critical section, and every
    20	    ownership check races the reclaim itself. So a crashed holder is never
    21	    stolen: waiters simply fail closed (``TimeoutError``) after
    22	    ``timeout_seconds`` rather than risk a double writer. This trades
    23	    availability for provable safety and only affects exotic non-POSIX hosts --
    24	    the supported Linux-cron deployment always takes the ``flock`` path, where
    25	    the kernel releases a crashed holder's lock automatically. A wedged non-POSIX
    26	    lock is cleared by removing the stale ``*.lock`` file.
    27	
    28	Standard library only. No trading logic, no network, no secrets.
    29	"""
    30	
    31	from __future__ import annotations
    32	
    33	import os
    34	import time
    35	from contextlib import contextmanager
    36	from pathlib import Path
    37	from typing import Generator, Union
    38	
    39	try:  # POSIX advisory file locking; absent on non-POSIX platforms.
    40	    import fcntl
    41	except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX fallback
    42	    fcntl = None
    43	
    44	DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0
    45	DEFAULT_POLL_SECONDS = 0.02
    46	
    47	
    48	@contextmanager
    49	def cross_process_lock(
    50	    lock_path: Union[str, Path],
    51	    *,
    52	    timeout_seconds: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
    53	    poll_seconds: float = DEFAULT_POLL_SECONDS,
    54	) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
    55	    """Hold an exclusive cross-process lock on ``lock_path`` for the block's body.
    56	
    57	    Uses ``fcntl.flock`` when available and a portable ``O_EXCL`` lock file
    58	    otherwise. Both honor ``timeout_seconds``: a waiter that cannot acquire within
    59	    the window raises ``TimeoutError`` (fail closed) rather than blocking forever
    60	    or stealing a possibly-live lock.
    61	    """
    62	    lock_path = Path(lock_path)
    63	    lock_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    64	    if fcntl is not None:
    65	        with _flock(lock_path, timeout_seconds, poll_seconds):
    66	            yield
    67	    else:  # pragma: no cover - exercised via monkeypatched fcntl in tests
    68	        with _portable_lock(lock_path, timeout_seconds, poll_seconds):
    69	            yield
    70	
    71	
    72	@contextmanager
    73	def _flock(lock_path: Path, timeout_seconds: float, poll_seconds: float) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
    74	    """POSIX critical section via ``fcntl.flock`` (kernel-released on crash).
    75	
    76	    Acquired non-blocking (``LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB``) in a poll loop so a hung holder
    77	    cannot block a waiter indefinitely; the blocking form would ignore
    78	    ``timeout_seconds``. Uncontended acquisition succeeds on the first attempt.
    79	    """
    80	    assert fcntl is not None
    81	    start = time.monotonic()
    82	    # Append mode: flock locks the file-table entry regardless of size, and "a"
    83	    # avoids truncating the sidecar on every acquisition.
    84	    with open(lock_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    85	        while True:
    86	            try:
    87	                fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
    88	                break
    89	            except OSError:
    90	                if time.monotonic() - start > timeout_seconds:
    91	                    raise TimeoutError(
    92	                        f"could not acquire flock on {lock_path} within {timeout_seconds:g}s"
    93	                    ) from None
    94	                time.sleep(poll_seconds)

    96	            yield
    97	        finally:
    98	            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    99

   101	@contextmanager
   102	def _portable_lock(lock_path: Path, timeout_seconds: float, poll_seconds: float) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
   103	    """Portable ``O_CREAT | O_EXCL`` lock. No reclaim: only the creator ever removes
   104	    it, so no process can delete another's lock; a crashed holder makes waiters
   105	    fail closed (``TimeoutError``) instead of risking a double writer."""
   106	    start = time.monotonic()
   107	    while True:
   108	        try:
   109	            fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
   110	            break
   111	        except FileExistsError:
   112	            if time.monotonic() - start > timeout_seconds:
   113	                raise TimeoutError(
   114	                    f"could not acquire lock {lock_path} within {timeout_seconds:g}s"
   115	                ) from None
   116	            time.sleep(poll_seconds)
   117	    try:
   118	        yield
   119	    finally:
   120	        os.close(fd)
   121	        try:
   122	            os.unlink(lock_path)
   123	        except FileNotFoundError:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
   124	            pass
   125	
   126	
   127	__all__ = ["cross_process_lock"]

   313	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
   314	        run: |
   315	          git config --global user.name "github-actions[bot]"
   316	          git config --global user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
   317	          gh auth setup-git
   318	
   319	          EXISTING_BRANCH="${{ steps.check_duplicates.outputs.existing_branch }}"
   320	          if [ -n "$EXISTING_BRANCH" ]; then
   321	            BRANCH="$EXISTING_BRANCH"
   322	            IS_UPDATE=true
   323	          else
   324	            BRANCH="selfheal-repair-$(date +%s)"
   325	            IS_UPDATE=false
   326	          fi
   327	          git checkout -b "$BRANCH"
   328	          git add .
   329	          git commit -m "[Self-Heal] Auto-repair drift"
   330	
   331	          TITLE="[Self-Heal Repair] Drift fixes"
   332	          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "workflow_run" ]; then
   333	            TITLE="[Self-Heal Reactive] CI fix"
   334	          elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "schedule" ]; then
   335	            TITLE="[Self-Heal Scheduled] Drift fixes"
   336	          elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
   337	            TITLE="[Self-Heal Manual] Repair"
   338	          fi

   340	          SCHEDULE=$(grep "^schedule:" .github/self-heal-schedule.yml | awk -F"'" '{print $2}' || echo "N/A")
   341	          RATIONALE=$(grep "^rationale:" .github/self-heal-schedule.yml | awk -F"'" '{print $2}' || echo "N/A")

   343	          # AGENTS.md's "Pull request expectations" requires a summary, the
   344	          # exact checks run, known limitations, and a secrets confirmation --
   345	          # the previous body left reviewers to reconstruct all of that from
   346	          # workflow logs (Codex review, PR #477). Built unconditionally (not just
   347	          # on first creation) so a force-pushed update to an already-open repair

   352	
   353	          **Trigger Reason:** ${{ github.event_name }}
   354	          **Current Schedule:** \`${SCHEDULE}\` (${RATIONALE})
   355	
   356	          **Summary:**
   357	          The automated self-heal pipeline detected and fixed drift in the repository. See the diff for the exact files changed.
   358	
   359	          **Checks run (scripts/healthcheck.py, before and after the repair):**
   360	          - \`ruff check .\`
   361	          - \`pytest --cov=. --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered --cov-fail-under=90\`
   362	          - \`python run_dca.py --demo --report --now 2026-08-03T15:45 --artifacts-dir <tmp dir>\`

   368	
   369	          **Secrets:** The guard step scanned the diff (tracked and newly-created files) for secret-shaped strings (\`api_key\`, \`token\`, \`password\`, \`secret\`, \`bearer\`) before this PR was opened; no matches were found. Human review is still required per this repo's PR expectations.
   370	
   371	          **Logs:**
   372	          - [View Artifact Logs](https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }})"
   373	
   374	          if [ "$IS_UPDATE" = "true" ]; then
   375	            # Push onto the already-open repair PR's branch (this workflow's
   376	            # own disposable branch) rather than opening a second PR.
   377	            git push --force-with-lease origin "$BRANCH"
   378	            # Refresh the PR body so it describes the commit reviewers now see,
   379	            # not the previous run's trigger reason and log link (Codex review,

   382	            echo "Pushed an additional fix to the existing repair PR ($BRANCH)."
   383	            exit 0
   384	          fi
   385	
   386	          git push --set-upstream origin "$BRANCH"
   387	
   388	          # Ensure required labels exist (mirrors compute-schedule.yml’s first-run hardening)

   391	            gh label create automation --description "Automated repository maintenance" --color ededed >/dev/null
   392	          fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Unified structured decision/reason codes for the daily DCA streams.
     3	
     4	The reliability plan calls for *structured reason codes* -- a single vocabulary
     5	of machine-readable strings that explain why a run, a per-symbol decision, or a
     6	safety gate produced the outcome it did (``NO_LOWER_PRICE``, ``ALREADY_FILLED``,
     7	``STALE_POINTER``, ``BROKER_HISTORY_INCOMPLETE``, ``SAFETY_CAP`` ...). Today
     8	those reasons are scattered across several modules under different spellings:
     9	
    10	  * :mod:`scripts.same_day_pointer` -- ``STATUS_STALE`` / ``STATUS_PENDING`` ...
    11	    (pointer freshness).
    12	  * :mod:`scripts.run_classification` -- the ``top_up_guard_result`` codes
    13	    (``no_prior_run``, ``price_not_below_prior_run``, ``incremental_top_up``,
    14	    ``no_incremental_difference``, ``missing_prior_price``).
    15	  * ``schemas/run_state.schema.json`` -- the ``order_submit_status`` enum.
    16	
    17	This module does NOT replace those (they remain the on-disk contract); it is the
    18	one place that *names* the plan's canonical reason codes, validates them, and
    19	bridges the existing lower-level codes onto the canonical set so ledger/metrics
    20	consumers can group heterogeneous outcomes without re-learning five vocabularies.
    21	
    22	Standard library only. No trading logic, no network, no secrets.
    23	"""
    24	
    25	from __future__ import annotations
    26	
    27	from typing import Dict, FrozenSet
    28	
    29	# --- Allocation / top-up decision outcomes -----------------------------------
    30	
    31	#: No prior same-day allocation for the symbol -> the full desired amount is a
    32	#: first allocation (not a top-up).
    33	FIRST_ALLOCATION = "FIRST_ALLOCATION"
    34	#: Prior allocation exists and the current price is strictly below the earlier
    35	#: reference price -> buy the incremental ``desired - effective_prior``.
    36	EFFECTIVE_TOP_UP = "EFFECTIVE_TOP_UP"
    37	#: Prior allocation exists but the current price is NOT below the earlier
    38	#: reference price -> no incremental buy (the top-up invariant blocked it).
    39	NO_LOWER_PRICE = "NO_LOWER_PRICE"
    40	#: The symbol's effective prior allocation already meets or exceeds the desired
    41	#: amount -> nothing left to buy.
    42	ALREADY_MET_OR_OVERFILLED = "ALREADY_MET_OR_OVERFILLED"
    43	#: The incremental top-up was computed but is below the broker minimum.
    44	BELOW_BROKER_MINIMUM_ORDER_SIZE = "BELOW_BROKER_MINIMUM_ORDER_SIZE"
    45	#: A same-day order/fill already exists for the symbol (duplicate guard).
    46	ALREADY_FILLED = "ALREADY_FILLED"
    47	#: Prior allocation exists but no comparable reference price is available ->
    48	#: conservatively buy $0 and flag for manual review.
    49	MISSING_PRIOR_PRICE = "MISSING_PRIOR_PRICE"
    50	#: No current decision price available -> cannot evaluate the top-up invariant.
    51	MISSING_CURRENT_PRICE = "MISSING_CURRENT_PRICE"
    52	
    53	# --- Safety / fail-closed blocks ---------------------------------------------
    54	
    55	#: Same-day broker order history could not be proven complete (pagination did
    56	#: not terminate cleanly, or an artifact order id was never resolved). The
    57	#: fail-closed outcome: do NOT buy rather than assume zero prior allocation.
    58	BROKER_HISTORY_INCOMPLETE = "BROKER_HISTORY_INCOMPLETE"
    59	#: A latest_* pointer was stale/prior-date/malformed and cannot be trusted as
    60	#: same-day scheduled evidence.
    61	STALE_POINTER = "STALE_POINTER"
    62	#: A per-symbol / daily / weekly exposure cap would be exceeded.
    63	SAFETY_CAP = "SAFETY_CAP"
    64	#: The configured broker account was not pinned/validated before reconciliation
    65	#: or submission.
    66	ACCOUNT_UNPINNED = "ACCOUNT_UNPINNED"
    67	#: Same-day broker coverage cannot be proven complete, so trading is locked out
    68	#: for the window (the incomplete-history lockout).
    69	INCOMPLETE_HISTORY_LOCKOUT = "INCOMPLETE_HISTORY_LOCKOUT"
    70	
    71	# --- Terminal / status outcomes ----------------------------------------------
    72	
    73	SUBMITTED = "SUBMITTED"
    74	SKIPPED = "SKIPPED"
    75	BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
    76	DRY_RUN = "DRY_RUN"
    77	NO_CANDIDATES = "NO_CANDIDATES"
    78	
    79	#: Every canonical reason code, for validation and enumeration.
    80	ALL_REASONS: FrozenSet[str] = frozenset(
    81	    {
    82	        FIRST_ALLOCATION,
    83	        EFFECTIVE_TOP_UP,
    84	        NO_LOWER_PRICE,
    85	        ALREADY_MET_OR_OVERFILLED,
    86	        BELOW_BROKER_MINIMUM_ORDER_SIZE,
    87	        ALREADY_FILLED,
    88	        MISSING_PRIOR_PRICE,
    89	        MISSING_CURRENT_PRICE,
    90	        BROKER_HISTORY_INCOMPLETE,
    91	        STALE_POINTER,
    92	        SAFETY_CAP,
    93	        ACCOUNT_UNPINNED,
    94	        INCOMPLETE_HISTORY_LOCKOUT,
    95	        SUBMITTED,
    96	        SKIPPED,
    97	        BLOCKED,
    98	        DRY_RUN,
    99	        NO_CANDIDATES,
   100	    }
   101	)
   102	
   103	#: Reason codes that mean "no buy happened / no buy should happen". Useful for
   104	#: ledger and metrics consumers that need to separate no-buy runs from buys.
   105	NO_BUY_REASONS: FrozenSet[str] = frozenset(
   106	    {
   107	        NO_LOWER_PRICE,
   108	        ALREADY_MET_OR_OVERFILLED,
   109	        BELOW_BROKER_MINIMUM_ORDER_SIZE,
   110	        ALREADY_FILLED,
   111	        MISSING_PRIOR_PRICE,
   112	        MISSING_CURRENT_PRICE,
   113	        BROKER_HISTORY_INCOMPLETE,
   114	        STALE_POINTER,
   115	        SAFETY_CAP,
   116	        ACCOUNT_UNPINNED,
   117	        INCOMPLETE_HISTORY_LOCKOUT,
   118	        SKIPPED,
   119	        BLOCKED,
   120	        NO_CANDIDATES,
   121	        # A dry run places no real order, so it is a no-buy outcome for any
   122	        # ledger/metrics consumer separating no-buy runs from actual purchases.
   123	        DRY_RUN,
   124	    }
   125	)
   126	
   127	#: Reason codes that represent a fail-closed safety block (as opposed to a
   128	#: benign no-buy such as NO_LOWER_PRICE). A window ending on one of these should
   129	#: be surfaced as blocked, not as a successful no-buy run.
   130	FAIL_CLOSED_REASONS: FrozenSet[str] = frozenset(
   131	    {
   132	        BROKER_HISTORY_INCOMPLETE,
   133	        STALE_POINTER,
   134	        SAFETY_CAP,
   135	        ACCOUNT_UNPINNED,
   136	        INCOMPLETE_HISTORY_LOCKOUT,
   137	    }
   138	)
   139	
   140	#: Bridge from :mod:`scripts.run_classification`'s ``top_up_guard_result`` codes
   141	#: (the on-disk ``top_up_guard_result`` enum in schemas/run_state.schema.json)
   142	#: onto the canonical vocabulary above, so a consumer reading either spelling
   143	#: can normalize to one set. ``incremental_top_up_amount`` returns the left-hand
   144	#: keys; :func:`from_top_up_guard` maps them to the right-hand canonical codes.
   145	_TOP_UP_GUARD_TO_CANONICAL: Dict[str, str] = {
   146	    "no_prior_run": FIRST_ALLOCATION,
   147	    "incremental_top_up": EFFECTIVE_TOP_UP,
   148	    "price_not_below_prior_run": NO_LOWER_PRICE,
   149	    "no_incremental_difference": ALREADY_MET_OR_OVERFILLED,
   150	    "below_broker_minimum_order_size": BELOW_BROKER_MINIMUM_ORDER_SIZE,
   151	    "missing_prior_price": MISSING_PRIOR_PRICE,
   152	    "missing_prior_base": MISSING_PRIOR_PRICE,
   153	}
   154	
   155	
   156	def is_valid_reason(code: str) -> bool:
   157	    """True when ``code`` is a canonical reason code."""
   158	    return code in ALL_REASONS
   159	
   160	
   161	def from_top_up_guard(guard_result: str) -> str:
   162	    """Map a ``top_up_guard_result`` code to the canonical reason vocabulary.
   163	
   164	    Unknown inputs are returned unchanged so a newly-added lower-level code is
   165	    surfaced verbatim rather than silently coerced to a wrong canonical value.
   166	    """
   167	    return _TOP_UP_GUARD_TO_CANONICAL.get(guard_result, guard_result)
   168	
   169	
   170	def is_fail_closed(code: str) -> bool:
   171	    """True when ``code`` is a fail-closed safety block (not a benign no-buy)."""
   172	    return code in FAIL_CLOSED_REASONS
   173	
   174	
   175	__all__ = [
   176	    "FIRST_ALLOCATION",
   177	    "EFFECTIVE_TOP_UP",
   178	    "NO_LOWER_PRICE",
   179	    "ALREADY_MET_OR_OVERFILLED",
   180	    "BELOW_BROKER_MINIMUM_ORDER_SIZE",
   181	    "ALREADY_FILLED",
   182	    "MISSING_PRIOR_PRICE",
   183	    "MISSING_CURRENT_PRICE",
   184	    "BROKER_HISTORY_INCOMPLETE",
   185	    "STALE_POINTER",
   186	    "SAFETY_CAP",
   187	    "ACCOUNT_UNPINNED",
   188	    "INCOMPLETE_HISTORY_LOCKOUT",
   189	    "SUBMITTED",
   190	    "SKIPPED",
   191	    "BLOCKED",
   192	    "DRY_RUN",
   193	    "NO_CANDIDATES",
   194	    "ALL_REASONS",
   195	    "NO_BUY_REASONS",
   196	    "FAIL_CLOSED_REASONS",
   197	    "is_valid_reason",
   198	    "from_top_up_guard",
   199	    "is_fail_closed",
   200	]
     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Writer for the model usage audit log (schemas/model_usage_log.schema.json).
     3	
     4	Implements the ``model_usage_log`` contract declared in
     5	``config/scheduled_tasks.json``: one append-only JSONL entry per run of a
     6	covered daily DCA task, recording which model / routing mode it used so
     7	cost-conscious model routing can be audited over time. See
     8	``docs/cost_tracking.md`` (Model usage log).
     9	
    10	This module has no knowledge of which LLM/agent is actually driving a given
    11	run -- Python code cannot introspect that. Per the manifest's
    12	``model_actual_not_exposed_rule``, callers that don't have that information
    13	should leave ``model_actual`` at its default (``'not_exposed'``) and rely on
    14	the ``model_requested``/``model_routing_mode`` defaults (cost-conscious),
    15	overriding them only when a caller genuinely knows better (e.g. an explicit
    16	premium escalation).
    17	
    18	Standard library only. Writing this log is always best-effort: a task's own
    19	scheduled run (safety-critical trading logic) must never fail or block
    20	because an audit-log append failed, so ``log_model_usage`` catches and logs
    21	every exception rather than raising into its caller.
    22	"""
    23	
    24	from __future__ import annotations
    25	
    26	import argparse
    27	import json
    28	import logging
    29	import sys
    30	from datetime import datetime, timezone
    31	from pathlib import Path
    32	from typing import Any, Dict, Mapping, Optional
    33	
    34	# This module is directly executable (``python scripts/model_usage_log.py
    35	# --run-id ...``, and its test is documented as runnable the same way), which
    36	# puts only ``scripts/`` on sys.path -- so the repo root is added here before
    37	# the shared helper below is imported, or the CLI dies with ModuleNotFoundError
    38	# before it can parse an argument (Codex review, PR #219: "Preserve direct
    39	# execution of the model-usage CLI"). Same bootstrap as
    40	# scripts/drift_detection.py.
    41	_REPO_ROOT = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
    42	if _REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:
    43	    sys.path.insert(0, _REPO_ROOT)
    44	
    45	from dca_paths import stream_root  # noqa: E402 - needs the sys.path setup above
    46	
    47	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    48	
    49	# Resolved at IMPORT time and kept only as the module's advertised default for
    50	# callers that read the constant. The functions below deliberately do NOT default
    51	# to it: $DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT set after this module was imported would leave
    52	# model-usage evidence appended under the old tree while the credit-usage
    53	# report, which resolves the shared root per call, scans the relocated one -- and
    54	# the run's usage then reads as MISSING (Codex review, PR #219). The bundled
    55	# morning and midday configs omit artifact_paths.model_usage_log_root, so their
    56	# loaders take this default path and would have inherited the same staleness.
    57	DEFAULT_LOG_ROOT = stream_root("model_usage")
    58	DEFAULT_MANIFEST_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "config" / "scheduled_tasks.json"
    59	
    60	REQUIRED_FIELDS = (
    61	    "run_id",
    62	    "task_name",
    63	    "scheduled_for_et",
    64	    "run_origin",
    65	    "stream",
    66	    "model_requested",
    67	    "model_actual",
    68	    "model_routing_mode",
    69	    "triggered_at_utc",
    70	    "artifact_path",
    71	)
    72	
    73	MODEL_ROUTING_MODE_VALUES = ("cost_conscious", "default", "premium")
    74	PREMIUM_REASONS = (
    75	    "failure_recovery",
    76	    "safety_validation",
    77	    "connector_debug_escalation",
    78	    "explicit_user_request",
    79	)
    80	
    81	
    82	class UnknownTaskError(LookupError):
    83	    """Raised when a cron_id/task_id is not a covered task in the manifest."""
    84	
    85	
    86	def _load_task_directory(manifest_path: str | Path) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]:
    87	    """Map task_id -> {"scheduled_for_et", "stream", "task_name"} from the
    88	    manifest's ``model_usage_log.applies_to_daily_tasks_et`` list -- the
    89	    single source of truth for which tasks are covered (see
    90	    config/scheduled_tasks.json)."""
    91	    manifest = json.loads(Path(manifest_path).read_bytes())
    92	    entries = manifest.get("model_usage_log", {}).get("applies_to_daily_tasks_et", [])
    93	    directory: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = {}
    94	    for entry in entries:
    95	        directory[entry["task_id"]] = {
    96	            "scheduled_for_et": entry["et"],
    97	            "stream": entry["stream"],
    98	            "task_name": entry["role"],
    99	        }
   100	    return directory
   101	
   102	
   103	def build_entry(
   104	    *,
   105	    run_id: str,
   106	    artifact_path: str | Path,
   107	    cron_id: Optional[str] = None,
   108	    task_id: Optional[str] = None,
   109	    task_name: Optional[str] = None,
   110	    scheduled_for_et: Optional[str] = None,
   111	    stream: Optional[str] = None,
   112	    run_origin: str = "scheduled",
   113	    model_requested: str = "cost_conscious_default",
   114	    model_actual: str = "not_exposed",
   115	    model_routing_mode: str = "cost_conscious",
   116	    reason_for_premium_model: Optional[str] = None,
   117	    triggered_at_utc: Optional[datetime] = None,
   118	    notes: Optional[str] = None,
   119	    manifest_path: str | Path = DEFAULT_MANIFEST_PATH,
   120	) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   121	    """Build one schema-valid model usage log entry.
   122	
   123	    ``task_name``/``scheduled_for_et``/``stream`` are looked up from the
   124	    manifest by ``task_id`` (or ``cron_id``) when not supplied directly, so
   125	    callers only need to pass the task's identifier plus run-specific facts
   126	    (run_id, artifact_path, run_origin). Raises ``UnknownTaskError`` if
   127	    neither identifier resolves to a covered task, and ``ValueError`` for any
   128	    other schema violation (missing field, bad enum, inconsistent premium
   129	    reason).
   130	    """
   131	    if not cron_id and not task_id:
   132	        raise ValueError("build_entry requires cron_id and/or task_id")
   133	    identifier = task_id or cron_id
   134	    assert identifier is not None
   135	
   136	    if task_name is None or scheduled_for_et is None or stream is None:
   137	        directory = _load_task_directory(manifest_path)
   138	        looked_up = directory.get(identifier)
   139	        if looked_up is None:
   140	            raise UnknownTaskError(f"{identifier!r} is not a covered task in {manifest_path}")
   141	        task_name = task_name or looked_up["task_name"]
   142	        scheduled_for_et = scheduled_for_et or looked_up["scheduled_for_et"]
   143	        stream = stream or looked_up["stream"]
   144	
   145	    if model_routing_mode not in MODEL_ROUTING_MODE_VALUES:
   146	        raise ValueError(f"invalid model_routing_mode {model_routing_mode!r}; expected one of {MODEL_ROUTING_MODE_VALUES}")
   147	    if model_routing_mode == "premium":
   148	        if reason_for_premium_model not in PREMIUM_REASONS:
   149	            raise ValueError(
   150	                f"reason_for_premium_model must be one of {PREMIUM_REASONS} when model_routing_mode='premium', "
   151	                f"got {reason_for_premium_model!r}"
   152	            )
   153	    elif reason_for_premium_model is not None:
   154	        raise ValueError(
   155	            f"reason_for_premium_model must be null/omitted when model_routing_mode={model_routing_mode!r}, "
   156	            f"got {reason_for_premium_model!r}"
   157	        )
   158	
   159	    triggered = triggered_at_utc or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   160	    triggered_str = triggered.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") if isinstance(triggered, datetime) else triggered
   161	
   162	    entry: Dict[str, Any] = {
   163	        "run_id": run_id,
   164	        "task_name": task_name,
   165	        "scheduled_for_et": scheduled_for_et,
   166	        "run_origin": run_origin,
   167	        "stream": stream,
   168	        "model_requested": model_requested,
   169	        "model_actual": model_actual,
   170	        "model_routing_mode": model_routing_mode,
   171	        "triggered_at_utc": triggered_str,
   172	        "artifact_path": str(artifact_path),
   173	    }
   174	    if cron_id:
   175	        entry["cron_id"] = cron_id
   176	    if task_id:
   177	        entry["task_id"] = task_id
   178	    if reason_for_premium_model is not None:
   179	        entry["reason_for_premium_model"] = reason_for_premium_model
   180	    if notes:

181	        entry["notes"] = notes
   182	
   183	    missing = [f for f in REQUIRED_FIELDS if not entry.get(f)]
   184	    if missing:
   185	        raise ValueError(f"model usage log entry missing required fields: {missing}")
   186	    return entry
   187	
   188	
   189	def resolve_log_path(triggered_at_utc: datetime, *, root: str | Path | None = None) -> Path:

    24	def register_secret(secret: str) -> None:
    25	    """Keep an in-process secret available to every console redaction boundary."""
    26	    if not secret:
    27	        return
    28	    if not isinstance(secret, str):
    29	        raise TypeError("registered console secrets must be text")
    30	    global _REGISTERED_SECRETS
    31	    with _REGISTERED_SECRETS_LOCK:
    32	        # The auth-file password must never be moved into the environment merely
    33	        # so the older environment-value pass below can find it: every console
    34	        # job inherits a copy of that environment.  Keep an immutable snapshot
    35	        # instead, and retain old values for the process lifetime so credential
    36	        # rotation cannot uncover a value already held by an exception or log
    37	        # buffer (Same Page round 1).
    38	        _REGISTERED_SECRETS = tuple(sorted({*_REGISTERED_SECRETS, secret}, key=len, reverse=True))

    41	def redact(text: str) -> str:
    42	    """Remove credential-shaped values before persisting or showing job output."""
    43	    from near_close_dca import _redacted_diagnostic_text
    44	
    45	    # HTTP handlers are threaded, and a future credential reload may register a
    46	    # replacement while another thread is formatting a failure.  Copy the
    47	    # immutable tuple under its small dedicated lock, then release the lock
    48	    # before the deliberately thorough diagnostic sanitizer runs (panel finding,
    49	    # round 3).  Longest-first replacement prevents an overlapping shorter
    50	    # secret from leaving the suffix of a longer one visible.
    51	    with _REGISTERED_SECRETS_LOCK:
    52	        registered = _REGISTERED_SECRETS
    53	    for secret in registered:
    54	        text = text.replace(secret, "[redacted]")
    55	    # Preserve multiline credential delimiters until the shared sanitizer sees them.
    56	    text = _redacted_diagnostic_text(text).replace("[REDACTED]", "[redacted]")
    57	    for name, value in os.environ.items():
    58	        if value and len(value) >= 6 and any(key in name.upper() for key in ("SECRET", "TOKEN", "PASSWORD", "API_KEY", "ACCOUNT_NUMBER")):
    59	            text = text.replace(value, "[redacted]")
    60	    text = re.sub(r'(?i)((?:account(?:_number)?|token|api_key|password|secret)[\s\"\x27:=]+)[^\s,}\"\x27]+', r'\1[redacted]', text)
    61	    text = re.sub(r"\b\d{6,12}\b", "[redacted-number]", text)

 31015	    silently swallowed as part of the first's label text -- the private

 31022	    dash runs are all considered, not skipped past), and attempts an
 31023	    anchored :data:`_ARMOR_MARKER` match at each. A non-marker "-----"
 31024	    (no BEGIN/END keyword immediately after) fails the anchored match in
 31025	    O(1) -- the keyword check is the very next thing the pattern tests

 31027	    markers stays linear, not quadratic.

 31042	def _find_armor_spans(text: str) -> List[Tuple[int, int, bool, bool]]:
 31043	    """Every ``-----BEGIN <label>-----...`` armor block in ``text`` as
 31044	    ``(start, end, is_private, is_closed)`` tuples, in document order,
 31045	    computed by an ITERATIVE left-to-right scan over
 31046	    :data:`_ARMOR_MARKER`'s matches -- never recursively, and never via a
 31047	    single monolithic regex matching a whole block (BEGIN, body, and
 31048	    END) in one shot. ``is_closed`` is True ONLY when the span's own end
 31049	    came from an actual matching END for this block's own label; it is
 31050	    False whenever no such END was found -- whether the scan ran off the
 31051	    end of the text with nothing left, or (for a non-private outer
 31052	    block) stopped early at a later, unrelated marker -- either way
 31053	    there was never a genuine footer for THIS block, so it is treated as
 31054	    UNCLOSED/footer-less (Codex review, PR #1249: "Keep outer armor
 31055	    unclosed at a nested BEGIN"). See
 31056	    :func:`_redacted_diagnostic_text_secrets_and_armor`'s own docstring
 31057	    for why that distinction matters there (Codex review, PR #1249:
 31058	    "Redact whitespace credentials after unclosed non-private armor").

 31061	    increasingly narrow family of regex-composition bugs trying to match
 31062	    a "BEGIN ... END-or-message-end" block directly: a footer-less block
 31063	    needed an unbounded lazy body scan, which was quadratic against
 31064	    adversarial input; bounding it broke long labels; a backreferenced
 31065	    footer fixed both, but a single COMBINED pattern still could not
 31066	    correctly decide, for a NON-private block with no real footer of its
 31067	    own, whether to keep scanning past a NESTED private-key block hiding
 31068	    in its swallowed remainder without either (a) never seeing that
 31069	    nested block at all, or (b) recursing into the swallowed text to
 31070	    look for it -- and recursion itself became its own bug (Codex
 31071	    review, PR #1249: "Replace recursive armor rescanning with an
 31072	    iterative scan" -- unbounded recursion depth on adversarial nested
 31073	    input risked `RecursionError`, which would abort the very
 31074	    failure-artifact write this redaction exists to make safe).

 31077	    BEGIN marker, its own span extends to whichever comes FIRST --
 31078	    another marker whose label matches (case-insensitively) for a

 31109	    labeled nested BEGIN (e.g. an outer "RSA PRIVATE KEY" containing a

     6

     8	    full 6-hour runner default before Actions kills it, and for a privileged
     9	    job that is an extended window holding a live secret for no reason;
    10	  * every workflow (or job) declares a ``concurrency`` policy with a
    11	    ``group`` and an explicit ``cancel-in-progress`` -- this repo's
    12	    convention is that PR/branch runs cancel a superseded run and ``main``
    13	    never does, since ``main``'s runs are the audit record of what landed;
    14	  * every ``actions/checkout`` step sets ``persist-credentials: false`` --
    15	    a checkout that keeps credentials leaves the token readable from git
    16	    config to every later step and any script it runs, including, in a
    17	    privileged job, PR-influenced tooling. The action's own default is
    18	    ``true``; this repo's convention is the opposite.

    21	a top-level key GitHub Actions ignores (the same trick already used for YAML
    22	anchor blocks in shared workflows), so it is a schema-legal escape hatch
    23	rather than a magic comment a YAML round-trip could silently drop:
    24	
    25	    x-policy-exceptions:

1	"""Deployment-relative artifact roots for every scheduled DCA stream.
     2	
     3	The live deployment writes all run artifacts under a single tree
     4	(``/home/user/workspace/cron_tracking`` in production, via an explicit
     5	``$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT`` export), one subdirectory per scheduled stream.
     6	Every stream module used to hardcode its own absolute path into a module
     7	constant, which put 15 copies of one deployment detail across
     8	``morning_dca``, ``midday_dca``, ``dca_alerts``, ``scripts/run_classification``,
     9	``scripts/same_day_pointer``, and ``scripts/model_usage_log`` -- against the
    10	"do not hard-code local absolute paths" rule in ``AGENTS.md``, and with no way
    11	to relocate the tree short of editing source.
    12	
    13	They now derive from :func:`cron_tracking_root`, which honours
    14	``$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT`` and otherwise returns
    15	:data:`DEFAULT_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT` -- a checkout-relative ``cron_tracking``
    16	directory, NOT the bundled production path above (Codex review: "Describe
    17	the actual unset artifact root"). An unconfigured checkout therefore writes
    18	artifacts under the repo instead of the production tree; production always
    19	sets ``$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT`` explicitly, so this only affects local/ad-hoc
    20	runs.
    21	
    22	**Resolution timing.** The stream constants below are module-level and therefore
    23	resolved once, at import. That matches the deployment (a cron entry exports the
    24	variable before Python starts) and it is why callers that need a *late* override
    25	-- ``dca_alerts.write_failed_start_marker``, the per-stream
    26	``DCA_*_LIVE_STATE_ROOT`` overrides in ``scripts/run_classification`` -- keep
    27	reading the environment at call time instead of relying on these.
    28	
    29	Standard library only; imports nothing from the rest of the project, so any
    30	module (including ``scripts/*``) can use it without creating a cycle. Mirrors
    31	:mod:`dca_fileio` in that respect.
    32	"""
    33	
    34	from __future__ import annotations
    35	
    36	import os
    37	from pathlib import Path
    38	from typing import Any
    39	
    40	# The bundled production tree serialized in config/*.json. This must remain
    41	# stable so rebase_bundled_root() can detect and rewrite those paths.
    42	BUNDLED_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT = "/home/user/workspace/cron_tracking"
    43	
    44	# Local default for an unconfigured checkout: keep run artifacts inside this
    45	# repository so the root exists on any machine and remains gitignored, rather
    46	# than falling back to a deployment-specific literal like
    47	# BUNDLED_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT (AGENTS.md: "never from a literal `/home/user/...`
    48	# string"). Production sets $DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT explicitly.
    49	DEFAULT_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT = str((Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "cron_tracking").resolve())
    50	
    51	# Deployment override, following the DCA_* convention already used by
    52	# DCA_CONFIG_DIR, DCA_ATTEMPT_LOG_ROOT, and DCA_INTRADAY_LIVE_STATE_ROOT.
    53	CRON_TRACKING_ROOT_ENV = "DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT"
    54	
    55	
    56	def cron_tracking_root() -> str:
    57	    """Root directory holding every per-stream artifact tree.
    58	
    59	    ``$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT`` when set and non-empty, else
    60	    :data:`DEFAULT_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT`. An empty variable is treated as unset so
    61	    a blank export cannot silently redirect artifacts to the filesystem root.
    62	
    63	    Trailing separators are stripped so every consumer derives the same string.
    64	    :func:`stream_root` joins through ``os.path.join``, which collapses them,
    65	    while :func:`rebase_bundled_root` concatenates -- so an export of
    66	    ``/srv/dca/`` produced ``/srv/dca/morning_dca`` from one and
    67	    ``/srv/dca//morning_dca`` from the other. Those compare unequal as strings,
    68	    and ``MorningDCAExecutor`` decides whether ``prior_allocation_roots`` is
    69	    still at its class default by exact tuple equality: a mismatch there makes a
    70	    default config look explicitly overridden, which skips the same-day manual
    71	    top-up context merge and lets a midday run re-buy a ticker an earlier manual
    72	    allocation already covered (Codex review, PR #219).
    73	
    74	    A root that is nothing but its root prefix keeps that prefix rather than
    75	    being trimmed away: ``"/"`` stays ``"/"``, and a Windows drive or UNC root
    76	    keeps its separator (``"C:\\"`` stays ``"C:\\"``). Trimming those would

   115	def rebase_bundled_root(value: Any) -> Any:

   120	    ``prior_allocation_roots``, the preflight resolution roots, …). Those values

   122	    from :func:`stream_root` -- meaning a deployment that set
   123	    ``$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT`` still had its executors read and write the
   124	    bundled production tree while everything reading ``dca_paths`` moved
   125	    (Codex review, PR #219: "Route loaded stream roots through the shared
   126	    override").
   127	
   128	    Rewriting the bundled prefix here keeps one source of truth without
   129	    templating ~40 config values. A path that does NOT sit under the bundled
   130	    root is deliberately returned untouched: an operator who wrote an explicit
   131	    absolute path into config meant that exact path.
   132	
   133	    The match is anchored at a path boundary -- the root itself, or the root
   134	    followed by a separator. A bare ``startswith`` also swallowed sibling
   135	    directories that merely share the prefix, so an explicitly configured
   136	    ``…/cron_tracking_backup/morning_dca`` was rewritten to
   137	    ``<root>_backup/morning_dca`` and the executor read or wrote a tree the
   138	    operator never named (Codex review, PR #219).
   139	
   140	    Both ``/`` and ``os.sep`` count as that boundary. The bundled paths are
   141	    serialized in ``config/*.json`` with forward slashes regardless of platform,
   142	    so keying the check on ``os.sep`` alone meant that on Windows -- where
   143	    ``os.sep`` is a backslash -- no descendant path ever matched, and setting the
   144	    override silently moved the module-derived constants while leaving the
   145	    executors on the bundled tree: readers and writers split across two roots
   146	    (Codex review, PR #219).
   147	
   148	    Typed ``Any`` rather than ``str`` on purpose: :func:`rebase_bundled_roots_in`
   149	    maps this over whole parsed config documents, so it is handed the ints,
   150	    bools, and ``None``s that sit alongside the paths and returns them
   151	    untouched. Annotating it ``str -> str`` described a narrower contract than
   152	    the function actually implements and than its only caller relies on
   153	    (Copilot review, PR #219).
   154	    """
   155	    if not isinstance(value, str):
   156	        return value
   157	    boundaries = {"/", os.sep}
   158	    if value != BUNDLED_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT and not any(
   159	        value.startswith(BUNDLED_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT + sep) for sep in boundaries
   160	    ):
   161	        return value
   162	    matched_root = BUNDLED_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT
   163	    configured = cron_tracking_root()
   164	    if configured == matched_root:
   165	        return value
   166	    suffix = value[len(matched_root) :]
   167	    # Rebuild with the PLATFORM separator instead of concatenating. The bundled
   168	    # values are serialized with forward slashes, so concatenation produced
   169	    # "C:\dca/morning_dca" on Windows while stream_root() -- which joins through
   170	    # os.path.join -- produced "C:\dca\morning_dca". Windows resolves both, but
   171	    # MorningDCAExecutor decides whether prior_allocation_roots is still at its
   172	    # class default by EXACT string equality, so the mismatch made a default
   173	    # config look explicitly overridden, skipping the same-day manual top-up
   174	    # merge and letting a midday run re-buy a ticker an earlier manual
   175	    # allocation already covered (Codex review, PR #219).

   183	def rebase_bundled_roots_in(node: Any) -> Any:
   184	    """Recursively apply :func:`rebase_bundled_root` to every string in ``node``.
   185

   187	    a loader happens to read today, so a path added to ``config/*.json`` later

   190	    are rewritten. Returns a new structure; the input is not mutated.
   191	    """

   193	        return {key: rebase_bundled_roots_in(value) for key, value in node.items()}

schemas/run_state.schema.json:66:      "description": "Overall order-submission outcome for the run. 'no_orders_submitted' (added 2026-07-27) is a run that fired, evaluated every ticker, and deliberately submitted nothing: a completed no-order run, neither a failure nor budget exhaustion. Its cause is carried by completion_reason (no ticker qualified on the ladder, so nothing reached the spread gate) or by error_class (candidates reached the spread gate and every one was failed closed there). See config/scheduled_tasks.json:spread_data_availability_policy. 'not_submitted_confirmation_required' means Robinhood review passed but submission was blocked by required post-review user confirmation: the run_state is still valid scheduled-run evidence that the task ran, but carries no order_id and is NOT evidence of an order/fill. 'blocked_placement_phase_unreachable' is the approved terminal state (added 2026-07-22) when the scheduled 3:20 live task planned orders but neither the saved compute module nor the approved fallback placement path (main live placement runner / direct connector) could place them: the run still proves the task fired and keeps planned rows in signals.csv, but is NOT evidence of an order/fill and carries error_class='placement_phase_unreachable'. A compute-only module that plans orders but never places them (error_class='placement_not_implemented_in_compute_module') is NOT a valid terminal state and must not be written as a completed scheduled run. The scheduled 3:20 PM live task always writes a run_state (and updates latest_scheduled_run.json) even when this is not 'submitted'. See docs/run_classification.md and config/run_classification.json."
schemas/run_state.schema.json:70:      "description": "Machine-readable failure class for a non-clean run. Open-ended free-form concrete code, intentionally NOT a closed enum: constraining it would reject legitimate existing failure-state artifacts. The morning/midday live runners emit 'missing_or_invalid_raw_inputs' on a raw-persistence failure (morning_dca.py), and the scheduled tasks also emit codes such as 'pointer_normalization_failed', 'missing_preflight_artifact', and 'no_incremental_top_up' (see config/scheduled_tasks.json and config/run_classification.json). The 3:20 placement contract (added 2026-07-22) additionally defines two placement-specific codes: 'placement_phase_unreachable' pairs with order_submit_status='blocked_placement_phase_unreachable' (approved terminal state after the fallback placement path was tried and failed); 'placement_not_implemented_in_compute_module' marks the Jul 22 2026 incident state (a compute-only module that planned orders but could not place them) and is NOT a valid terminal state for the pre-authorized scheduled live task -- validate_run_artifacts / the 3:40 watchdog reject it. Other concrete codes such as 'connector_error', 'safety_rejection', 'account_rejection', 'order_rejection', and 'recovery_failure' may also appear. 'scheduled_run_startup_failure' (added 2026-07-27) marks a scheduled live run that raised before reaching any writer; it still writes the complete root-level artifact set, which proves the slot fired but is never order evidence and never valid scheduled evidence. 'degraded_market_data' (added 2026-07-27) marks a zero-order run that completed while market-data providers were raising: its tickers degraded to NO_DATA/manual review rather than being genuinely evaluated, so the result is not a clean ladder no-op and must not be read as one. 'partial_placement_failure' (added 2026-07-27) marks a batch where some orders were submitted and at least one other placement raised. 'scheduled_run_failed_after_submission' (added 2026-07-27) marks a run that raised AFTER at least one order was submitted, kept distinct from the startup class so a consumer grouping by error_class never reports a late post-trade failure as startup trouble. 'missing_spread_data' (added 2026-07-27) is recorded ONLY when candidates actually reached the spread gate and every one was failed closed there; a run where no ticker qualified on the ladder never reached the gate and records completion_reason='no_ladder_candidates' with a null error_class instead. Null/omitted for clean runs and for a completed no-order run."
schemas/run_state.schema.json:74:      "description": "Outcome classification for the run, distinct from the nested run_classification identity object and never a substitute for it (that object stays a non-null object on every scheduled run). 'completed_no_orders' is a run that completed and deliberately submitted nothing; 'failed_after_connector_native_recovery_attempt' is a genuine placement failure after placement WAS attempted; 'failed_scheduled_run_startup' is a run that raised or was blocked before reaching placement at all, kept distinct so reporting cannot misattribute a startup, data, or precondition failure as a broker-placement failure; 'failed_after_partial_submission' covers both a run that raised AFTER submitting at least one order and a partially submitted batch where another ticker's placement failed, so the outcome never contradicts a non-zero orders_submitted_count and a failed placement is never dropped; 'failed_placement' is the manual-run equivalent of failed_after_connector_native_recovery_attempt, since the manual path never runs the scheduled connector-native recovery policy."
schemas/run_state.schema.json:78:      "description": "Why a COMPLETED run submitted no orders. 'no_ladder_candidates' means no ticker qualified on the ladder and same-day top-up rules, so nothing ever reached the spread gate and error_class stays null. 'blocked_before_spread_gate' means candidates DID qualify on the ladder but every one was stopped by a budget/cap/ceiling/duplicate check that runs before the spread lookup, so none carries a spread verdict. 'no_qualifying_orders_after_safety_checks' means candidates reached the spread gate but none cleared every check. 'date_or_holiday_gate_blocked' marks the date/holiday gate stub. Set on a completed_no_orders run; a failed run records error_class instead."

   162	 "severity":"high","first_seen_utc":"…","last_seen_utc":"…","occurrences":3,"collector_version":1}
   163	```
   164	
   165	**Redaction runs on `excerpt` and `signature` before either is written anywhere**, using a
   166	`redact()` lifted from `dca_console_jobs.py`'s rules and extended with: the literal value of
   167	`$ROBINHOOD_AGENTIC_ACCOUNT_NUMBER` when set, every env value whose *name* matches the
   168	existing regex, `~` substitution, and the `\b\d{6,12}\b` rule. A unit test asserts a
   169	synthetic account number planted in a fixture never appears in any emitted artifact.
   170	
   171	Raw, unredacted incidents are written under `$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT/self_heal/incidents/`
   172	— already gitignored — so the operator can still read the full crash locally.
