   174	## Component 3 — `scripts/incident_ledger.py`
   175	
   176	Append-only JSONL under `$DCA_CRON_TRACKING_ROOT/self_heal/ledger/incidents.jsonl`, with a
   177	sanitized mirror at `diagnostics/ledger.jsonl` on the diagnostics branch. Every append takes
   178	`file_lock.cross_process_lock`. A compacted `diagnostics/index.json` holds current state per
   179	fingerprint so a reader need not replay the whole log.
   180	
   181	Per-fingerprint state machine:
   182	
   183	```
   184	   new ──dispatch──▶ dispatched ──PR merged & healthcheck green──▶ repaired
   185	    │                    │
   186	    │                    ├──repair produced no diff, or CI still red──▶ refused ──▶ (back to new, attempts+1)
   187	    │                    │
   188	    └────────────────────┴──attempts > max_attempts_per_fingerprint──▶ quarantined (terminal)
   189	```
   190

191	`quarantined` is terminal and is **never** dispatched again. It is surfaced in the digest
   192	and in the daily report so a human sees it. Clearing it is an explicit operator action
   193	(`--unquarantine <fingerprint>`).
   194	
   195	Novelty verdict: a fingerprint is dispatch-eligible iff state ∈ {`new`, `refused`} **and**
   196	`attempts < max_attempts_per_fingerprint`.
   197	
   198	## Component 4 — `scripts/self_heal_governor.py` (the limits)
   199	
   200	`evaluate(now, ledger, config, spend) -> Decision`. `Decision` is
   201	`(dispatch: bool, fingerprint: str | None, reason: str)`, where `reason` is a constant from
   202	a new `scripts/self_heal_reasons.py` following the `scripts/reason_codes.py` house pattern.
   203	Checks run in this fixed order and **short-circuit on the first refusal**:
   204	
   205	| # | Gate | Config key | Default | Refusal reason |
   206	|---|---|---|---|---|
   207	| 0 | Kill switch | `enabled` / `$DCA_SELF_HEAL_DISABLED` | `true` / unset | `DISABLED` |
   208	| 1 | Self-origin drop | — | — | `SELF_ORIGIN_DROPPED` |
   209	| 2 | Daily rate limit | `max_runs_per_day` | **1** | `RATE_LIMITED_DAILY` |
   210	| 3 | Circuit breaker | `consecutive_failure_threshold`, `breaker_cooldown_hours` | **3**, **72** | `BREAKER_OPEN` |
   211	| 4 | Per-fingerprint attempts | `max_attempts_per_fingerprint` | **3** | `FINGERPRINT_QUARANTINED` |
   212	| 5 | Token/USD budget | `daily_token_budget`, `daily_usd_budget`, `monthly_usd_budget` | **200000**, **2.00**, **20.00** | `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_TOKENS` / `_USD` |
   213	| 6 | Actions minutes | `monthly_actions_minutes` | **300** | `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_MINUTES` |
   214	| 7 | Wall clock | `max_wall_clock_seconds` | **1800** | `WALL_CLOCK_EXCEEDED` |
   215	| 8 | Novelty | — | — | `NO_NOVEL_INCIDENTS` |
   216	
   217	Every evaluation — dispatch or refusal — is appended to the ledger with its reason, so the
   218	answer to "why did nothing happen yesterday?" is always in the record.
   219	
   220	**Loop prevention, stated explicitly.** Four independent mechanisms, any one of which alone
   221	halts a runaway:
   222	
   223	- Gate 2 caps *dispatches per day* at 1. Even a pathological collector that mints a new
   224	  fingerprint every minute gets one dispatch.
   225	- Gate 4 caps *attempts per failure identity* at 3 for that identity's entire lifetime, then
   226	  quarantines it permanently.
   227	- Gate 3 trips a breaker after 3 consecutive unsuccessful dispatches regardless of
   228	  fingerprint, and holds it open for 72 hours or until an explicit human reset.
   229	- Gate 1 drops any incident whose origin path is under `diagnostics/`, whose branch matches
   230	  `selfheal-*`, or whose signature names a self-heal module — so the loop cannot observe
   231	  and react to its own exhaust. (The workflow's existing `!startsWith(github.ref_name,
   232	  'selfheal-')` guard covers the ref; this covers the *content*.)
   233	
   234	Fail-closed: an unparseable `config/self_heal.json`, an unreadable ledger, a clock that has
   235	moved backwards relative to the last ledger entry, or a governor exception all produce
   236	`dispatch=False` with an explicit reason. There is no code path where an error yields
   237	permission.

1	# The PR review workflow: trust boundary and migration note
     2	
     3	Two workflow files implement the automated Antigravity PR review:
     4	
     5	* **`.github/workflows/antigravity-pr-review.yml`** ("Antigravity PR Review
     6	  (Analyze)") -- unprivileged, triggered on `pull_request`. Checks out the PR
     7	  head, computes the diff against the base branch, and uploads it as an
     8	  artifact along with the PR number and head SHA. Holds no secret, no
     9	  `pull-requests` permission, nothing beyond `contents: read`.
    10	* **`.github/workflows/antigravity-pr-review-post.yml`** ("Antigravity PR
    11	  Review (Post)") -- privileged, triggered on `workflow_run` when the analyze
    12	  workflow completes. Holds `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `pull-requests: write`.
    13	  Validates that the triggering run is genuinely what it claims to be, then
    14	  cross-checks artifact metadata, computes its own diff from the validated
    15	  immutable base/head commits, generates the review, and posts the comment.
    16	
    17	## Why two workflows
    18	
    19	A `pull_request`-triggered workflow's own YAML is taken from the **PR's head
    20	branch**. A contributor who can push a branch can edit that workflow file in
    21	their PR, and the edit takes effect in their own run -- including deleting a
    22	safety step, or replacing the command a later step runs. This repo's earlier
    23	single-workflow design tried to compensate for that by restoring
    24	`.github/scripts/` from the base branch immediately before running the
    25	reviewer script, and hardened that restore step across several review rounds
    26	(removing added files, not just overlaying changed ones; failing closed when
    27	the base branch has nothing to restore; `set -euo pipefail`). Each of those
    28	fixes was correct and necessary, but all of them were mitigating symptoms of
    29	the same root cause: the workflow doing the mitigating was itself editable by
    30	the thing it was defending against.
    31	
    32	`workflow_run` does not have that problem. GitHub always runs the version of
    33	a `workflow_run`-triggered workflow's YAML that lives on the repository's
    34	**default branch**, regardless of what the triggering run's branch contains.
    35	A PR cannot edit `antigravity-pr-review-post.yml` and have that edit apply to
    36	its own review -- an edit there only takes effect once merged. That is a
    37	structural property of the trigger, not a runtime check that could be
    38	bypassed by removing the check.
    39	
    40	## What the privileged workflow still has to defend against
    41	
    42	Moving the secret to a `workflow_run` job does not, by itself, make it safe --
    43	it just changes what has to be verified:
    44	
    45	1. **The job must never check out PR-head code.** `workflow_run` fixes *which
    46	   version of the workflow file runs*, but a checkout step inside that file
    47	   could still be pointed at the PR's branch via `ref:`, which would check out
    48	   attacker-influenced code into a job holding the API key. The `review`
    49	   job's checkout step has no `ref:` at all -- omitting it checks out
    50	   `github.sha`, which for a `workflow_run` event is the default branch's
    51	   current commit. The PR still reaches this job, but only as the diff
    52	   **text**, computed from fetched commit objects, never as code that gets
    53	   executed. The full-history fetch uses checkout's ephemeral authentication;
    54	   `persist-credentials: false` still removes that authentication afterward.
    55	2. **The triggering run's identity must be validated, not assumed.** The
    56	   `workflows:` filter on the trigger restricts by name at GitHub's level, but
    57	   the job re-validates explicitly: the triggering workflow's name, that its
    58	   event was `pull_request`, that it succeeded, that its head repository is
    59	   this repository (not a fork), and that it has an associated PR. Any
    60	   failure here is logged per-check and fails the job (`validate-provenance`
    61	   in the workflow file).
    62	3. **A downloaded artifact cannot establish which code was reviewed.**
    63	   `actions/download-artifact` fetches by run ID; the job cross-checks the
    64	   artifact's own recorded PR number, head SHA, and base SHA against the
    65	   validated values, catching wrong-run or malformed metadata. The analyzer
    66	   can still substitute arbitrary diff text with correct metadata. Trusted
    67	   consumer code therefore validates both SHAs as available commit objects
    68	   and computes its own diff into `trusted_review_input/diff.patch`, which
    69	   is the reviewer's only workflow input. The downloaded diff remains
    70	   diagnostic data. Both paths use explicit base/head SHAs, with a two-dot
    71	   fallback only for disconnected histories. External diff programs and
    72	   text conversion are disabled; no PR code is checked out or executed.
    73	
    74	`scripts/tests/test_pr_review_workflow_trust_boundary.py` encodes all three of
    75	these as structural assertions against the workflow YAML -- not just that the
    76	right steps exist, but that they are wired in the order and with the
    77	dependencies that make the properties above actually hold. It fails loudly,
    78	naming the specific thing that drifted, if any of them regress.
    79

    98	## Workflow policy checks
    99	
   100	The trusted reviewer install and CI dependency audit share
   101	`requirements-pr-review.txt`. The SDK remains exactly pinned; CI resolves
   102	and audits its full transitive graph for both supported Python versions
   103	alongside the research dependencies. Resolution disables source builds and
   104	does not run the reviewer SDK.
   105	
   106	`scripts/workflow_policy.py` statically enforces three org-wide policies
   107	against every file in `.github/workflows/*.yml`, run as ordinary pytest tests
   108	(`scripts/tests/test_workflow_policy.py`) rather than a separate CI job:
   109	
   110	* every job sets `timeout-minutes`;
   111	* every workflow (or job) declares a `concurrency` block with a `group` and
   112	  an explicit `cancel-in-progress`;
   113	* every `actions/checkout` step sets `persist-credentials: false`.
   114	
   115	A workflow file can declare an explicit, reasoned exception via a top-level
   116	`x-policy-exceptions` key (GitHub Actions ignores unrecognized top-level keys,
   117	the same mechanism already used for YAML anchor blocks in shared workflows):
   118	
   119	```yaml
   120	x-policy-exceptions:
